insights.insight: Crinkl has crossed 90,182 cryptographically verified receipts representing $4.77M in confirmed consumer spend — a deterministic purchase dataset, not a modeled proxy audience.

The network is processing ~389 verified receipts per day at a structurally consistent pace across a two-week observation window, with afternoon UTC intervals (around 16:15) showing the highest intraday throughput — suggesting a reliable, not bursty, data supply.

Seven-day verified GMV is running at roughly $97K–$101K per week across ~2,400 receipts, giving brand planners a concrete, auditable spend volume to underwrite targeting against rather than estimated reach figures.

At current BTC pricing, each verified receipt carries a ~$0.10 payout to the submitting consumer — a cost-per-confirmed-purchase signal that sits well below the $5+ CPM brands pay for probabilistic inference on purchase intent.

A verified receipt confirms a purchase occurred at a specific retailer; probabilistic targeting infers purchase intent from behavioral signals that correlate loosely with buying. For CMOs evaluating cookieless alternatives, that evidentiary gap — inference versus cryptographic proof — is the core due-diligence question.
